title: Immunohistological analysis of endometrial BCL6 expression (B-cell lymphoma cells), uterine natural killer cells (uNK), and plasma cells (CD138+) in the endometrium before and after surgical treatment of uterine fibroids.
summary:
The present study aims to systematically identify and evaluate immunological and molecular changes in the endometrium of women with symptomatic uterine fibroids following surgical treatment. The focus lies on three key markers: the transcriptional repressor BCL6, uterine natural killer cells (uNK cells, CD56+), and plasma cells (CD138+), which are considered indicators of chronic endometritis.
This study is intended to provide a basis for further hypotheses regarding the immunomodulatory effects of different fibroid therapies and their relevance for endometrial regeneration.

interventions.name: Women aged 18 years and older of reproductive age with fibroid-related symptoms who decide to undergo surgery (laparoscopy or transcervical, ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation using Sonata®) due to the fibroid(s).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
non
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnant and breastfeeding women are not allowed to participate in the study. Women of childbearing potential must use a reliable method of contraception during the menstrual cycle in which the study examinations take place. If there is a reasonable suspicion of pregnancy, the examinations for the study cannot be performed.
